newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice's Fenice opera house to be rebuilt by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Venice's Fenice opera house to be rebuilt by 2000.

text.p: Venice's historic La Fenice opera house, destroyed by fire last January, will be rebuilt exactly as it used to be, the lagoon city's mayor said on Friday.
Mayor Massimo Cacciari said work to rebuild the 204-year-old La Fenice, Italian for the phoenix, would begin next January and would be completed by November 1999.
Investigators suspect January's blaze may have been arson but have yet to complete their inquiry.

Cacciari told a news conference in Rome that reconstruction work would cost at least 120 billion lire ($78.2 million) but the city had only about half of the money and would be forced to borrow the rest.
He said the city had received some five billion lire ($3.26 million) from private donors but "we are not even close to where we need to be with regard to funding."
He added that the destruction of the opera house was a "painful wound" that had yet to heal.
The theatre, which held priceless memories as the stage for premieres of some of Italy's most famous operas, opened in 1772 and was rebuilt after a fire in 1836. ($1=1,534 lire)
